blocks.content: This chapter covers J&K-specific development projects and flagship infrastructure — an area of heavy recent investment given the government's post-2019 emphasis on visible development as part of its broader integration narrative for the UT.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Infrastructure and connectivity projects serve as flagship initiatives to accelerate national modernization.
Welfare and social schemes provide targeted support for inclusive socio-economic development.
Tourism and investment promotion drive regional growth and bolster economic opportunities.
Quick revision points summarize key objectives, ministries, and beneficiaries of central government schemes.

cells: Major national infrastructure project connecting the Kashmir Valley to the Indian rail network for the first time; includes the Chenab Bridge (the world's highest railway arch bridge, standing higher than the Eiffel Tower) and the Anji Khad Bridge (India's first cable-stayed rail bridge); substantially completed and formally inaugurated with through-services in recent years, a landmark all-weather connectivity achievement
Under-construction all-weather road tunnel beneath the Zoji La Pass (Chapter 2/3), intended to end the historic seasonal winter closure of the Srinagar-Leh road link
Modernised all-weather road connectivity through the Pir Panjal, reducing dependence on the older, more accident-prone Jawahar Tunnel route
Major healthcare infrastructure expansion, part of a wider push to establish new medical colleges and super-speciality hospital facilities across the UT
New Central Sector Industrial Development Scheme incentives introduced to attract manufacturing and other investment following the removal of Article 35A's land-purchase restrictions (Chapter 14)

blocks.content: ★ EXAM POINT: The Chenab Bridge (part of USBRL) — the world's highest railway arch bridge, taller than the Eiffel Tower — is one of the most frequently cited infrastructure superlatives associated with modern J&K, alongside the Anji Khad Bridge as India's first cable-stayed rail bridge.

items: Central flagship schemes (Ayushman Bharat health insurance, PM Awas Yojana housing, Jal Jeevan Mission for piped water supply, and others) have been extended and actively promoted across J&K UT, with the UT administration periodically highlighting saturation/coverage milestones in official communications.

Back-to-Village (B2V) programme — a J&K-specific outreach initiative launched to bring government officials and services directly to panchayat/village level, aimed at improving grassroots governance responsiveness and public-grievance redressal.

Special employment and skill-development schemes targeting Kashmir Valley youth have been a recurring policy emphasis, alongside continued reservation and rehabilitation provisions for displaced Kashmiri Pandit and PoJK-displaced communities (Chapter 19).

Since 2019, the UT administration has actively promoted J&K as an investment and tourism destination, citing the removal of Article 35A's land-purchase restrictions as opening new opportunities, alongside dedicated tourism-infrastructure investment (new ropeways, upgraded pilgrimage-route facilities, and promotion of lesser-visited destinations such as Gurez and Bangus Valley) intended to diversify beyond the traditional Gulmarg-Pahalgam-Sonamarg circuit.

G20-linked events hosted in Srinagar in 2023 (during India's G20 presidency) were widely publicised by the government as signalling a return to international-level normalcy and confidence in the region, though the event itself, like other J&K-related developments, drew a mix of domestic and international commentary.

USBRL (Udhampur-Srinagar-Baramulla Rail Link): connects Kashmir Valley to the national rail network; includes the Chenab Bridge (world's highest railway arch bridge) and Anji Khad Bridge (India's first cable-stayed rail bridge).
Zoji La Tunnel (under construction): aims to end winter closure of the Srinagar-Leh road via the Zoji La Pass.
Back-to-Village (B2V) programme: J&K-specific grassroots governance outreach initiative.
G20-linked meeting hosted in Srinagar (2023) during India's G20 presidency, publicised as a normalcy/confidence signal.
